page.layout: Running head at top, centred: "HISTORIA MOTUUM", with page number "24" at the top left. One column of running text filling the page, from the first line to the last full line. No marginal notes, no footnotes, no catchword.

main_text.p: Calvinum, fanaticum illum Puritanum (nam hifce clogiis ab Hierarchicis, heroes illi vulgo appellan-tur) videbunt ad partes vocatum, & magisteriali vir-gula flagellatum, quod aufus fuerit fanctiffimum papam Antichristum vocare, quod nulla spiritualis communio, cum idololatrica illa Ecclesia Romana, habenda sit, quod non expectata ordinatione Genevensis Episcopi aufus sit cathedram paftoralem Genevae confcendere, licet petitus votis civium & fuffragiis honorabilium, quod hoc fuo audaci coepto viam ftraverit aliis, praesertim Iohanni Knoxio Scoti difcipulo, qui non expectata Episcoporum ordinatione (qui tunc intentiffimis animis Christi teneram Ecclesiam in Scotia diflipabant) aufus fit pro Paftore fe gerere, licet a plebe petitus (quam maxime poteftatem habere, vel eligendi dignos Sacerdotes, vel indignos recufandi, atque illud de Divina authoritate defcendere, olim teftatus eft Cyprianus) & a legitimo presbytero Iohanne Rough ordinatus: etenim ii jure Divino ordinatio Paftorum Episcopis competit, totus fere beatus chorus reformatorum injuftae intrufionis rei pera-gentur, & mirandum illud divinae benignitatis opus in Ecclesiis reformandis in dubium vocabitur. Audiet etiam alia majoris momenti, quam iniquè fcilicet & rigidè fe gesserit Augustinus contra Semipelagianos: Calvinus & Genevenses contra Castalionem, Synodus Dordracena contra Remonstrantes, quam utile sit Imagines in templis locare, signo crucis signari, coram altari genu flectere, quam nullius momenti sint controversiae, inter reformatos & Pontificios agitatae, quam facilis partium reconciliatio, nisi paucorum puritanorum obstaret pertinax morositas. Verebantur etiam ad haec Scoti, ne sub obscuris ejusmodi verborum involucris, ea Ecclesiis Scoticis obtruderentur, quae alibi hactenus publicè

page.notes: Show-through and the edge of the neighbouring page along both margins (dark marks at the right and left edges) were left out. The text is one unbroken paragraph running over the full page. Words in italics were read from the scan and may be slightly off in the italic/roman boundary. "Iohanni Knoxio Scoti" and "Iohanne Rough" were read as printed. The final line "publicè" is set short and right-aligned, as printed.
